strings.name: Dilip Shanghvi
strings.role: Founder and Executive Chairman of Sun Pharma
strings.summary: Dilip Shanghvi is an Indian entrepreneur who founded Sun Pharma in 1983 and helped expand it from a psychiatry medicines business into a multinational pharmaceutical company. His work spans strategy, acquisitions and research investment; he remained Executive Chairman after handing over the Managing Director role in 2025.
strings.coverageNote: Checked through November 17, 2026, with recent evidence from the October 30 earnings call transcript. The Organon acquisition was still pending then; expected completion in early 2027 was forward-looking. Conflicting birth dates are recorded at October 1955 precision.
strings.influence.rationale: Founded Sun Pharma and developed India’s generic and specialty medicines business through drug research and acquisitions.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: Bachelor of Commerce from the University of Calcutta; Managing Director in company biographies is a management role, not a medical degree.
strings.facts.f2.label: Division of responsibilities
strings.facts.f2.value: He is Executive Chairman, while Kirti Ganorkar is Managing Director; Shanghvi continues to discuss strategy and R&D and has not fully retired.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Research investment
strings.highlights.h1.text: On the October 2026 call, he reported quarterly R&D investment of INR7.784 billion, or 4.8% of sales; spending and pipelines do not establish clinical success or drug approval.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Quality and regulation
strings.highlights.h2.text: The FDA records a 2017 permission-to-resume-operations letter and a 2023 non-compliance letter for Mohali. Post-acquisition quality obligations matter, but facility actions must not be described as Shanghvi’s personal conviction.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Discusses research and acquisition progress
strings.timeline.t1.text: He discussed R&D investment on the earnings call; the company said Organon remained separately listed and closing conditions were still outstanding.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Organon acquisition agreement announced
strings.timeline.t2.text: The April 26 announcement in US Eastern time corresponds to April 27 in India; the offer was $14 per share in cash, with $11.75 billion representing enterprise value, not a personal purchase price.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Hands over Managing Director role
strings.timeline.t3.text: Kirti Ganorkar succeeded him while Shanghvi remained Executive Chairman; June 13 was the earlier announcement date.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Concert acquisition completed
strings.timeline.t4.text: Sun Pharma expanded its research portfolio; the candidate drug in the announcement was still investigational, and closing the acquisition did not mean drug approval.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Receives Padma Shri
strings.timeline.t5.text: India’s government listed him as a Padma Shri recipient in Trade and Industry.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Ranbaxy merger completion announced
strings.timeline.t6.text: The release described the start of business integration; its announcement date is distinct from legal effectiveness and retrospective accounting dates.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Company launches IPO
strings.timeline.t7.text: Sun Pharma entered the public capital market through an IPO; this was not its founding year.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Founds Sun Pharma
strings.timeline.t8.text: The company began with five psychiatry products and a two-person marketing team, then gradually expanded.
